Throughout, $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$ is a
[[probability-spaces|probability space]], $X,Y$ are
[[random-variables|random variables]] and $\mathbb{E}$ denotes
[[expectation]]. We build conditional expectation in three steps: given an
event, given a σ-algebra, and finally as an orthogonal projection, which
makes precise the idea of the best prediction of $Y$ from partial
information.

## Conditioning on an event

Let $F\in\mathcal{F}$ with $\mathbb{P}(F)>0$.

:::{.definition data-title="Conditional probability and expectation given an event"}

The **conditional probability given $F$** is, for every $E\in\mathcal{F}$,
$$
\mathbb{P}_{F}(E)=\mathbb{P}(E\mid F):=\frac{\mathbb{P}(E\cap F)}{\mathbb{P}(F)}.
$$
It is a probability measure, so $(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P}_{F})$ is a new
probability space. Random variables are unchanged but have a new
distribution. For $X$ with $\mathbb{E}|X|<\infty$ the **conditional
expectation given $F$** is the expectation under $\mathbb{P}_F$:
$$
\mathbb{E}[X\mid F]:=\int_{\Omega}X\,d\mathbb{P}_{F}
=\frac{1}{\mathbb{P}(F)}\int_{F}X\,d\mathbb{P}
=\frac{\mathbb{E}[X\mathbb{1}_{F}]}{\mathbb{P}(F)}.
$$

:::

If $\mathbb{P}(F)=0$ we may set $\mathbb{P}_F\equiv0$ and extend the notions
trivially. The **conditional distribution function** of $X$ given $F$ is
$$
F_{X|F}(x)=\mathbb{P}(X\leq x\mid F)=\frac{\mathbb{P}(\{X\leq x\}\cap F)}{\mathbb{P}(F)},
$$
and when it is differentiable its derivative $f_{X|F}$ is the conditional
density, so that $\mathbb{E}[X\mid F]=\int x f_{X|F}(x)\,dx$.

## Conditioning on a σ-algebra

Conditioning on a single event only uses one yes/no piece of information. We
now condition on a whole σ-algebra of observable events.

### Countable partitions

Let $\{F_{n};n\geq1\}$ be a countable partition of $\Omega$ (disjoint sets
with union $\Omega$, each of positive probability) and let $\mathcal{G}$ be
the σ-algebra generated by it. By countable additivity,
$$
\mathbb{P}(E)=\sum_{n}\mathbb{P}(F_{n})\mathbb{P}_{F_{n}}(E),\qquad
\mathbb{E}[X]=\sum_{n}\mathbb{P}(F_{n})\mathbb{E}[X\mid F_{n}].
$$
Define the simple random variable
$$
\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}](\omega):=\sum_{n}\mathbb{E}[X\mid F_{n}]\,
\mathbb{1}_{F_{n}}(\omega),\qquad\omega\in\Omega.
$$
It is $\mathcal{G}$-measurable and for every $\Lambda\in\mathcal{G}$ (a union
of partition elements)
$$
\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}]\mathbb{1}_{\Lambda}\big]
=\mathbb{E}[X\mathbb{1}_{\Lambda}],
$$
and in particular $\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}]]=\mathbb{E}[X]$.
This identity is what generalises.

### General definition

:::{.definition data-title="Conditional expectation given a σ-algebra"}

Let $\mathcal{G}\subseteq\mathcal{F}$ be a sub-σ-algebra and $X$ an
integrable random variable. The **conditional expectation of $X$ given
$\mathcal{G}$** is the (a.s. unique) $\mathcal{G}$-measurable integrable random
variable $\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}]$ such that
$$
\mathbb{E}\big[X\mathbb{1}_{\Lambda}\big]
=\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}]\mathbb{1}_{\Lambda}\big],
\qquad\text{for all }\Lambda\in\mathcal{G}.
$$
For $E\in\mathcal{F}$ the **conditional probability of $E$ given
$\mathcal{G}$** is $\mathbb{P}(E\mid\mathcal{G}):=\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{1}_E\mid\mathcal{G}]$,
the $\mathcal{G}$-measurable random variable with values in $[0,1]$ such that
$$
\mathbb{P}(E\cap\Lambda)=\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{P}(E\mid\mathcal{G})\mathbb{1}_{\Lambda}\big],
\qquad\Lambda\in\mathcal{G}.
$$

:::

Existence and uniqueness follow from the [[radon-nikodym-derivative]]: the
signed measure $\Lambda\mapsto\mathbb{E}[X\mathbb{1}_\Lambda]$ is absolutely
continuous with respect to $\mathbb{P}$ on $\mathcal{G}$, and
$\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}]$ is its density. Section 4 gives a second
construction by projection.

### Conditioning on a random variable

For a random variable $Z$ we write
$\mathbb{E}[X\mid Z]:=\mathbb{E}[X\mid\sigma(Z)]$, where $\sigma(Z)$ is the
[[generated-sigma-algebra|σ-algebra generated by $Z$]]. By the Doob-Dynkin
lemma, $\mathbb{E}[X\mid Z]=h(Z)$ for some Borel function $h$.

If $(X,Z)$ has joint density $f_{X,Z}$ and $f_Z(z)>0$, the **conditional
density** and **conditional distribution function** of $X$ given $Z=z$ are
$$
f_{X|Z}(x\mid z)=\frac{f_{X,Z}(x,z)}{f_{Z}(z)},\qquad
F_{X|Z}(x\mid z)=\int_{-\infty}^{x}f_{X|Z}(u\mid z)\,du,
$$
and then $h(z)=\int x f_{X|Z}(x\mid z)\,dx$.

## Conditional expectation as a projection

Conditional expectation is the best prediction of $Y$ given partial
information, in the mean-square sense. This uses the Hilbert space structure
of square-integrable random variables.

:::{.definition data-title="Hilbert space"}

An [[inner-product-space|inner product space]] is a real vector space
$\mathcal{V}$ with a symmetric, bilinear, positive-definite map
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:\mathcal{V}\times\mathcal{V}\to\mathbb{R}$; it
induces the norm $\lVert v\rVert=\sqrt{\langle v,v\rangle}$. A **Hilbert
space** is an inner product space that is complete in this norm: every
Cauchy sequence converges to an element of $\mathcal{V}$. See
[[hilbert-spaces]].

:::

For a closed subspace $\mathcal{V}_1\subseteq\mathcal{V}$ and $v\in\mathcal{V}$,
the distance from $v$ to $\mathcal{V}_1$ is
$d=\inf_{v_1\in\mathcal{V}_1}\lVert v-v_1\rVert$, and the minimiser $v_1^*$ is
the **orthogonal projection** of $v$ onto $\mathcal{V}_1$.

:::{.theorem data-title="Projection theorem"}

If $\mathcal{V}_1$ is a closed subspace of a Hilbert space $\mathcal{V}$, then
for every $v\in\mathcal{V}$ there is a unique $v_1^*\in\mathcal{V}_1$ with
$\lVert v-v_1^*\rVert\leq\lVert v-v_1\rVert$ for all $v_1\in\mathcal{V}_1$, and
this is equivalent to the orthogonality condition
$$
\langle v-v_1^*,v_1\rangle=0\qquad\text{for all }v_1\in\mathcal{V}_1.
$$

:::

Now take $\mathcal{V}=L^2(\Omega,\mathcal{F},\mathbb{P})$, the space of
random variables with $\mathbb{E}[X^2]<\infty$, with inner product
$\langle X,Y\rangle=\mathbb{E}[XY]$ (see [[lp-spaces]]). For a
sub-σ-algebra $\mathcal{G}$, the set of $\mathcal{G}$-measurable square
integrable random variables is a closed subspace. For $\mathcal{G}=\sigma(X)$
it equals $A_X=\{h(X):h\text{ Borel},~\mathbb{E}[h(X)^2]<\infty\}$.

:::{.theorem data-title="Conditional expectation is the best prediction"}

For $Y\in L^2$ and $\mathcal{G}\subseteq\mathcal{F}$, the orthogonal
projection of $Y$ onto the $\mathcal{G}$-measurable subspace is
$\mathbb{E}[Y\mid\mathcal{G}]$, so
$$
\mathbb{E}\big[(Y-\mathbb{E}[Y\mid\mathcal{G}])Z\big]=0,\qquad
\lVert Y-\mathbb{E}[Y\mid\mathcal{G}]\rVert=\min_{Z\in L^2(\mathcal{G})}\lVert Y-Z\rVert.
$$
In particular $\mathbb{E}[Y\mid X]$ is the best mean-square predictor of $Y$
from $X$.

:::

:::{.proof}

By the projection theorem let $Y^*$ be the projection. Taking $Z=\mathbb{1}_\Lambda$
with $\Lambda\in\mathcal{G}$ in the orthogonality condition gives
$\mathbb{E}[Y\mathbb{1}_\Lambda]=\mathbb{E}[Y^*\mathbb{1}_\Lambda]$, and $Y^*$ is
$\mathcal{G}$-measurable, so $Y^*=\mathbb{E}[Y\mid\mathcal{G}]$ a.s. by the
uniqueness in the definition.

:::

## Properties

Let $\mathcal{G},\mathcal{G}_1,\mathcal{G}_2$ be sub-σ-algebras of
$\mathcal{F}$. Assuming the variables below are integrable (or square
integrable where indicated), the following hold almost surely.

1. **Linearity.**
   $\mathbb{E}[\alpha X+\beta Y\mid\mathcal{G}]=\alpha\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}]+\beta\mathbb{E}[Y\mid\mathcal{G}]$.
2. **Measurable variables.** If $X$ is $\mathcal{G}$-measurable then
   $\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}]=X$; in particular constants are unchanged.
3. **Independence.** If $X$ is independent of $\mathcal{G}$ then
   $\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}]=\mathbb{E}[X]$.
4. **Monotonicity.** If $X\leq Y$ then
   $\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}]\leq\mathbb{E}[Y\mid\mathcal{G}]$.
5. **Expectation.** $\mathbb{E}[\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}]]=\mathbb{E}[X]$.
6. **Taking out what is known.** If $X$ is $\mathcal{G}$-measurable and $XY$
   is integrable then $\mathbb{E}[XY\mid\mathcal{G}]=X\mathbb{E}[Y\mid\mathcal{G}]$.
7. **Monotone convergence.** If $0\leq X_n\uparrow X$ then
   $\mathbb{E}[X_n\mid\mathcal{G}]\uparrow\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}]$ (see
   [[monotone-convergence-theorem]]).
8. **Dominated convergence.** If $X_n\to X$ a.s. and $\lvert X_n\rvert\leq W$
   with $\mathbb{E}[W]<\infty$ then
   $\mathbb{E}[X_n\mid\mathcal{G}]\to\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}]$ (see
   [[dominated-convergence-theorem]]).
9. **Tower property.** If $\mathcal{G}_2\subseteq\mathcal{G}_1\subseteq\mathcal{F}$
   then
   $$
   \mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}_1]\mid\mathcal{G}_2\big]
   =\mathbb{E}\big[\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}_2]\mid\mathcal{G}_1\big]
   =\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}_2]
   $$
   (the smaller σ-algebra always wins).
10. **Jensen's inequality.** For convex $g$ with $g(X)$ integrable,
    $\mathbb{E}[g(X)\mid\mathcal{G}]\geq g(\mathbb{E}[X\mid\mathcal{G}])$ (see
    [[jensen-inequality]]).
